classification.difficultyReason: Explain general subset relationships using the definitions of intersection, union and the empty set.

content.prompt: Explain why the following statements are true, where $A$ and $B$ are any two sets.

answer.short: Every element of $A\cap B$ belongs to $A$.
answer.worked: The intersection $A\cap B$ contains only elements belonging to both $A$ and $B$. Every one of these elements therefore belongs to $A$, so $A\cap B\subseteq A$.

answer.short: Every element of $A\cap B$ belongs to $B$.
answer.worked: The intersection $A\cap B$ contains only elements belonging to both $A$ and $B$. Every one of these elements therefore belongs to $B$, so $A\cap B\subseteq B$.

answer.short: The union $A\cup B$ contains every element of $A$.
answer.worked: The union $A\cup B$ contains all elements belonging to $A$ or $B$, including those belonging to both. Thus every element of $A$ belongs to $A\cup B$, so $A\subseteq A\cup B$.

answer.short: Every element common to $A$ and $B$ also belongs to their union.
answer.worked: An element of $A\cap B$ belongs to both $A$ and $B$. The union $A\cup B$ includes elements belonging to either set or both sets. Hence every element of $A\cap B$ belongs to $A\cup B$, so $A\cap B\subseteq A\cup B$.

answer.short: The empty set is a subset of every set, including $A\cap B$.
answer.worked: The empty set has no elements, so it has no element outside $A\cap B$. It is therefore a subset of $A\cap B$.

answer.short: The empty set is a subset of every set, including $A\cup B$.
answer.worked: The empty set has no elements, so it has no element outside $A\cup B$. It is therefore a subset of $A\cup B$.
